newsitem.title: USA: Audio King won't open new stores in FY97.
newsitem.headline: Audio King won't open new stores in FY97.

text.p: Audio King Corp, citing its loss for the fiscal year ended June 30, said it does not plan to open any new stores in fiscal 1997 or undertake any major remodeling projects.
The consumer electronics retailer operates 11 specialty stores -- eight in Minnesota, one in South Dakota and two in Iowa.

On Tuesday it reported a fiscal 1996 loss of $0.09 per share compared with a year-ago profit of $0.23 per share. During the fourth quarter, it posted a loss of $0.28 per share compared with a year-earlier loss of $0.03 per share.
"Audio King's fourth quarter and yearend results were disappointing and did not meet expectations," said president Gary Thorne in a statement.

"The loss for the quarter was the result of failing to achieve planned sales and gross margin, which were requirements for profitability with Audio King's expanded sales square footage and increased fixed costs. Our slowdown in sales was consistent with a variety of factors adversely affecting the consumer electronics industry, which has also suffered a sales slowdown," Thorne added.

He cited double-digit price deflation of key product categories, rising consumer debt, a lack or delay of new products and product categories, higher levels of competition and lower margins as inventories were built up and markdowns were taken.
"The consumer electronics industry is strong, and I am confident that new products and technologies will revitalize the industry in 1997," Thorne noted.
